From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@healthsync.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: security@healthsync.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Upstream vendor graph + escrow question for SOC2/SIG

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the SOC2 pack you sent last week — that was helpful. Our InfoSec team has one follow-up: they need a map of upstream vendors (transitive dependencies) that Redwood relies on for inference and storage, and confirmation whether any critical components (model artifacts, backups, encryption keys) are held in an escrow or custodian arrangement.

Specifically, can you provide:
- A CSV listing each upstream vendor, the service they provide (e.g., model hosting, key management, artifact storage), and whether Redwood considers them a subprocessor or an indirect (transitive) dependency.
- Any certificates or attestations confirming custody/escrow for long-term model artifacts or encryption key escrow arrangements.
- A short note on whether any of these vendors have access to unredacted customer inputs at rest or in transit.

We need this to complete a SIG-lite and our procurement checklist — target delivery by Dec 10 if possible.

Appreciate it,
Emily
Emily Tran
Security Manager, HealthSync

Subject: Transitive vendor graph + escrow confirmations (pack)

Hi Emily — attaching the consolidated package per your request. Quick summary:

Attachments included:
- transitive-vendor-graph.csv (CSV): vendor list, service, transitive flag, access_note, kms_owner, escrow_status
- escrow-certification-redwood.pdf (PDF): signed attestation from our custodian partner for archived model artifacts; notes scope and retention window
- SOC2-SIG-evidence-index.md (MD): index to SOC2 control references and which file in this package maps to each SIG question

Highlights / short answers:
- Model artifacts: archived model artifacts are stored with our custodian partner (Vanguard Hosting) under a documented escrow arrangement for disaster recovery. See escrow-certification-redwood.pdf.
- KMS: Root customer encryption keys are customer-managed where requested (for Private deployments). For hosted accounts, Redwood-managed keys are used with HSM-backed KMS; internal key access is restricted to platform automation. No third-party has direct access to unredacted customer payloads except for limited telemetry processors that operate on anonymized aggregates (listed in the CSV).
- Transitive vendors: CSV flags vendors as SUBPROCESSOR (direct contractual relationship) or TRANSITIVE (indirect dependency). We included an "access_note" describing whether the vendor may touch unredacted inputs.

If you want a short walkthrough, I'm happy to schedule a 30-min review with your InfoSec team. Otherwise, please confirm receipt and if anything else is required for your SIG-lite.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
